title: Self-Guided Resilience-Building Energy Management to Enhance Well-being (RENEW) Intervention for People With Systemic Sclerosis (SSc)
off: Self-Guided Resilience-Building Energy Management to Enhance Well-being Intervention for People With Systemic Sclerosis: A Feasibility Study
collabs: National Institute on Disability, Independent Living, and Rehabilitation Research
summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to gather information on the RENEW app used by people with scleroderma. Specifically, the researchers want to learn more about RENEW by collecting information about the rates of recruitment, retention of study participants information about study completion, and time spent accessing the app content.
desc: RENEW is Institutional Review Board approved as a non-significant risk device but it not subject to 510(k) and therefore not regulated by the FDA.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Have a diagnosis of systemic sclerosis including: diffuse cutaneous SSc, limited cutaneous SSc, overlap, or SINE
* Have access to a reliable, internet-connected device (e.g. smartphone or tablet)
* Be able to read, speak, and understand English
* Participants need to report a score of at least 4 on a scale of 0 - 10 of fatigue severity, a cut-off for at least moderate fatigue in other fatiguing conditions1

Exclusion Criteria:

* Complex, unstable health issues that would preclude full participation in the study
* Planning to start new treatment for fatigue, pain, mood during the study period
* Previous experience with RENEW app or past participant of RENEW

arms.d: Individuals with SSc who are interested and eligible will undergo an informed consent process and will be given access to the RENEW program via the app

primary.m: Feasibility based on study recruitment rate

pubs.cit: Chen YT, Harper AE, Alore M, Haro E, Morris JT, Khanna D, et al. 'It helps me stay on track': patient experiences using a mobile app for self-management of systemic sclerosis with a focus on fatigue in women. Rheumatol Adv Pract. 2026. doi: 10.1093/rap/rkag102

abstracts:
Chen YT, Harper AE, Alore M, Haro E, Morris JT, Khanna D, et al. 'It helps me stay on track': patient experiences using a mobile app for self-management of systemic sclerosis with a focus on fatigue in women. Rheumatol Adv Pract. 2026. doi: 10.1093/rap/rkag102
OBJECTIVES: Fatigue is common and burdensome in people with systemic sclerosis (SSc), significantly impacting daily functioning and quality of life. Yet, it remains inadequately addressed in clinical care. This study aimed to explore participants' experiences using the RENEW (Resilience-building Energy Management to Enhance Well-being) mobile app as a standalone self-paced intervention without peer coaching for fatigue self-management.
METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with participants with SSc following completion of the 12-week RENEW mobile app intervention. Interviews were analysed using RADaR (Rigorous and Accelerated Data Reduction) technique in combination with thematic content analysis.
RESULTS: Fifteen women were included in the analysis (mean age 56 years ± 10), which reflects the higher prevalence of SSc among women. Among participants, 53% had limited SSc, while the remaining had diffuse SSc or overlap, and 40% had been diagnosed with SSc for less than 5 years (short duration). Four themes were identified: (1) the RENEW app and its features were intuitive; (2) the RENEW app's content enhanced the learning experience; (3) the RENEW app became a partner to support SSc self-management and (4) refinements to the app could enhance the patient experience.
CONCLUSION: The RENEW app was perceived as a relevant and user-friendly tool for supporting fatigue self-management in SSc. Findings suggest that a standalone app-based approach may offer a scalable option for fatigue self-management in SSc, while also highlighting areas for refinement to improve engagement and long-term use.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: clinicaltrials.gov, NCT07402863.

x.titre: RENEW : application d'autogestion de l'énergie et de la fatigue dans la sclérodermie systémique
x.question: Une application d'autogestion de la fatigue (RENEW) est-elle réalisable chez des patients atteints de sclérodermie systémique ?
x.contexte:
La fatigue est un symptôme fréquent et invalidant de la sclérodermie systémique, souvent associée à la douleur et à l'humeur dépressive. Les options thérapeutiques non médicamenteuses sont peu développées et l'accès aux programmes encadrés est limité.

RENEW est un programme d'autogestion proposé via une application mobile, centré sur la gestion de l'énergie et le renforcement de la résilience. Il est accessible à distance, sans accompagnement en personne.

Cette étude de faisabilité à un seul bras, menée à l'Université du Michigan (financement NIDILRR), évalue l'acceptabilité plutôt que l'efficacité : taux de recrutement, rétention à 12 semaines et temps passé dans l'application. Elle précède un éventuel essai randomisé. Les participants ont une fatigue au moins modérée (≥ 4/10). Le dispositif est considéré comme à risque non significatif et n'est pas soumis à une réglementation de la FDA.
x.interet: Elle prépare un essai d'efficacité d'une intervention numérique accessible, mais ne permet pas de conclure sur le bénéfice de RENEW sur la fatigue.
x.profil: Des adultes atteints de sclérodermie systémique avec une fatigue au moins modérée.
inclusion: Sclérodermie systémique (cutanée diffuse, limitée, chevauchement ou sine)
Accès à un appareil connecté (smartphone ou tablette)
exclusion: Problèmes de santé complexes ou instables empêchant la participation
Début prévu d'un nouveau traitement de la fatigue, de la douleur ou de l'humeur

bras.traitement: Programme d'autogestion via l'application RENEW, 12 semaines

x.critere: Faisabilité : taux de recrutement et rétention des participants à 12 semaines
x.resultats: Des entretiens semi-dirigés ont été menés après les 12 semaines d'utilisation de l'application RENEW, sans accompagnement par des pairs. Quinze femmes ont été analysées (âge moyen 56 ± 10 ans) ; 53 % avaient une sclérodermie limitée, les autres une forme diffuse ou un syndrome de chevauchement, et 40 % avaient un diagnostic datant de moins de 5 ans. Quatre thèmes sont ressortis : l'application et ses fonctions étaient intuitives, son contenu enrichissait l'apprentissage, elle devenait un partenaire pour l'autogestion de la sclérodermie, et des améliorations pouvaient en renforcer l'expérience. Les auteurs concluent que l'application est perçue comme pertinente et facile d'usage pour gérer la fatigue, et qu'une approche autonome par application pourrait être une option extensible, avec des points à affiner pour favoriser l'engagement à long terme.
